name: Bengal Sultanate
summary: An independent Muslim sultanate in Bengal, rich from rice, cotton and trade; it built brick mosques and supported Bengali literature until the Mughals conquered it (1576).

knownFor.label: Adina Mosque
knownFor.note: One of the largest mosques in South Asia.

location.value: The Bengal delta: today’s Bangladesh and West Bengal.

terrain.value: The Ganges–Brahmaputra delta, rivers and floodplains.

climate.value: Monsoon, with heavy rains and floods.

resources.value: Rice, cotton and silk; the article describes cotton and silk stuffs shipped from Bengal.

population.value: The article gives no regional total; Gaur had about 200,000 people around 1500.

urbanisation.value: Capitals at Pandua and Gaur; port of Chittagong.

disease.value: Cholera and fevers in the delta.

economicBase.value: Rice farming, fine textiles and sea trade.

tradeRoutes.value: Bay of Bengal trade to China and Southeast Asia.

wealth.value: Europeans and Ming China called Bengal “the richest country to trade with”; Portuguese observers compared Gaur with Lisbon.

moneyAndTax.value: Silver taka coins bearing the sultan’s name; large transactions were in silver taka.

inequality.value: Rulers and military elites above farmers and herders.

keyRulers.value: Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah (unified the delta; 1352 is tagged citation needed). Alauddin Hussain Shah (gained control in 1494).

succession.value: Ilyas Shahi, Hussain Shahi and other dynasties; frequent palace coups.

stability.value: Four usurper sultans from the Abyssinian (Habshi) mercenary corps ruled 1487–1494.

armyAndTech.value: War elephants, archers and river fleets.

majorWars.value: Akbar defeated the last sultan at the Battle of Raj Mahal, 12 July 1576 (infobox).

territoryChange.value: Chittagong became a seaport and trading hub; the article gives the conquest as 1340 in the text and 1512–1516 in the infobox.

alliancesRivals.value: Delhi, the Mughals, Mrauk U and the Ming (embassies under Zheng He).

inventions.value: No major inventions; famous for fine muslin weaving.

religion.value: Muslim rulers over a Hindu majority; Islam spread among farmers in the east.

languageWriting.value: Bengali and Persian; Bengali became a court language, and Bengali Muslim writers translated works such as the Thousand and One Nights.

artsArchitecture.value: The Adina Mosque was built under Sikandar Shah, with a design based on the Great Mosque of Damascus.

socialStructure.value: Muslim nobles, Hindu landholders and farmers.

sharedIdentity.value: A Bengali regional identity across faiths.

neighbours.value: Delhi Sultanate, Mughals, Mrauk U, Kamarupa.

ideasReligions.value: Sonargaon was a centre of Sufi education; Nur Qutb Alam, a court scholar, is named.

riseSignals.value: Ilyas Shah emerged victorious by 1352 and unified the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna deltas (the article tags 1352 citation needed).

peakPeriod.value: Hussain Shahi dynasty (1494–1538 in the dynasty table; other dates in the article vary).

declineSignals.value: Sher Shah Suri conquered Bengal (the infobox dates the invasion 1539; the dynasty list gives 1538).

outcome.value: Akbar defeated the last sultan at Raj Mahal in 1576; Mughal Bengal follows.

overallCertainty.value: Main events are known from chronicles; population figures are estimates.
